title: Gochujang Chicken Thighs with Soju Pan Sauce
summary: Cold-pan, skin-on chicken thighs painted with gochujang and finished in the oven. Served with a ginger, shallot and soju pan sauce sharpened with cucumber pickle juice, quick pickled cucumbers, crispy crushed potatoes and gochujang mayo.

steps.text: Lightly salt two skin-on chicken thighs per person. Just before cooking, dab off any excess moisture.
Lay them skin side down in a cold pan with no oil. Start on low heat, about 2 out of 10, to render out the skin fat.
As they brown they unstick from the pan; then flip them.
Paint with a good amount of gochujang and put them in the oven for 5–10 minutes, until 75 °C inside.
Ahead of time, thinly slice the cucumbers. Add a good amount of rice wine vinegar, some sugar and some salt, and mix.
After about 15 minutes, pour off the pickle juice that has collected and keep it for the pan sauce.
Finish the cucumbers with Korean chili flakes, toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.
Pour off about 80% of the fat from the chicken pan (keep it in the fridge for other cooking).
Add the diced shallots on low heat. When they turn translucent, grate in fresh ginger and cook for about a minute, then do the same with the garlic.
Once it smells fragrant, add gochujang. Keep the heat low or the sugar in it will burn.
Deglaze with soju (sake or white wine also work). Cook it down until jammy: a spatula drawn through it should leave a trail.
Add chicken stock or kombu dashi and reduce by half.
Add the cucumber pickle juice and reduce by half again to concentrate the tang.
Take it off the heat and stir in butter until melted.
Boil the new potatoes ahead of time.
Crush them on a tray by pressing a second tray on top, for as much crispy surface as possible.
Drizzle with olive oil and roast at 200 °C for 30 minutes until golden and crispy.
While the potatoes roast, mix mayo, gochujang, rice wine vinegar, toasted sesame oil and honey.
Spoon the pan sauce onto the plate and set the gochujang thighs on top.
Add the cucumbers, crushed potatoes and gochujang mayo, then finish with sesame seeds and fresh coriander.

notes: This is the third video in the creator's “two-ingredient chicken” series: just salt and gochujang on the chicken.
The video shows the whole method. The written recipe with exact quantities is on eatlikeanadult.com behind a $5/month membership.
gaps: Most quantities are spoken loosely (“some”, “a good amount”); none are shown on screen.
The oven temperature for the chicken isn't given; the 200 °C is for the potatoes.

source.quantity_basis: Spoken only (from the YouTube captions). No recipe text shows on screen.
